pr.title: Skip the Check workflow for changes that touch only docs or the site
pr.head: 93c1edaf6107e6ff3d7502480261c8dc5a7af6f8

summary: The Check workflow, .github/workflows/check.yml, is trip's CI. It runs two macOS jobs: check, which runs rustfmt, the release script's tests, clippy, the test suite, a build, and the end-to-end scripts, and msrv, which builds on the minimum supported Rust version. Before this change it ran on every pull request and every push to main, even one that only edited the README.

This pull request adds a paths-ignore filter to the pull_request and push triggers. When every file a change touches is a Markdown file, or sits under docs/ or site/, or is LICENSE, GitHub starts no run. A change that touches even one other file runs both jobs as before. The workflow_dispatch trigger, which the Release workflow uses to run Check on its release branch, gets no filter.

Skipping a run is safe only because nothing requires these checks. The main ruleset requires pull requests and linear history but no status checks. If check or msrv ever became required, a docs-only pull request would wait forever for a check that never starts, and the comment added above the filter says so.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• paths-ignore: a GitHub Actions trigger filter. GitHub skips the workflow only when every changed file matches one of its patterns.
  • Required status check: a check a branch rule makes a merge wait for. A check whose workflow never starts stays pending, so it blocks the merge.
  • Ruleset: GitHub's branch rules for main in this repository, read with gh api repos/ninjudd/trip/rulesets.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• Projector reviewed 93c1eda and found it clean, with no finding threads.
  • The review confirmed that no ruleset or branch protection on main requires a status check.

groups.title: The Check workflow's trigger filter
groups.kicker: Skip CI for changes to documentation, the site, and the license
intro: The whole change is six lines at the top of check.yml: the same paths-ignore list on both the pull_request and the push trigger, and a comment that explains it.

GitHub matches a pull request's filter against the pull request's whole diff, not only the newest push. So a pull request that already changes code keeps running Check after a docs-only push to it. On main, each squash-merged commit is matched on its own, so a docs-only merge starts no run.

files.note: Adds the same four-pattern paths-ignore to the pull_request and push triggers, and a comment saying the filter works only while no ruleset requires these checks.

checks.text: The comment records the one condition that would make this filter harmful: a required check on a skipped run waits forever. If you make check or msrv required later, replace the filter with a first job that reports success for docs-only changes.

Nothing the check or msrv job runs reads an ignored file. The review searched src/, tests/, and Cargo.toml and found no include_str!, no readme or license-file key, and no Markdown fixture. The one test that writes a README.md, in tests/install_e2e.py, writes it into its own temporary directory.

Every file that should still trigger a run falls outside the patterns: Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, src/, tests/, install.sh, .github/workflows/, and .github/scripts/release.py. **/*.md also matches Markdown at the repository root, such as README.md and AGENTS.md. A YAML parse of the file showed both triggers carry the list, with push still limited to main.
The release flow does not depend on a filtered run. release.yml runs Check on the release branch through workflow_dispatch, which has no filter, and its publish job never reads Check's result.
